item.title: Re: A Photo Book of Murderers
item.content:encoded:
1) There are plenty of stories, between trepanning, lobotomy, and the various eugenics tactics, so there should be plenty of fun in that regard. There should be plenty of additional stories in a universe where people sacrifice to eldritch horrors.

2) The basic problem is that you delve too much into the hook and not enough into the photobooks themselves. There are no mechanics on how it works, how a killer is determined for the person in question, not even if it is permanent or temporary. You have an interesting idea, but the item itself just isn't described to any degree. Heck, there's not even a lot of history given on it, and what little history there is doesn't really set it up.

3) In that regard, you have way too much hook. In fact, most of the central narrative is nothing but hook. Summarize it and add it to the hook section, and then go back and build your central narrative. You've got a great hook; you just need some actual details.

This is actually a fun idea, as weird as I know that sounds. While there are a number of Kid-TV SCP's, this is just different enough from them that it could work.

1) You need to flesh it out a bit. There's just nothing really here; it's just a skeleton. To whom or what the sacrifice is to needs to be better defined. 2) The UIU doesn't hand cases off to The Foundation without a good reason. Why did they do that this time?

It's an excellent start, it just needs some fleshing out.

item.title: Re: An atavistic humanoid + a mysterious organization
item.content:encoded:
1) You need to seriously cut down the number of words; Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook, and Additional Notes need to be about 400 words. You can eliminate the additional notes: You don't need names and you may want to drop the idea for an organization (more on that below). That's your first 43 words.

2) You may want to look into the current GOI to find a group that works for you. The obvious suggestions are Herman Fuller's Circus of the Disquieting (using a program to create circus freaks), Prometheus Labs (one group could be interested in developing prehistoric individuals to test some theories), or even a Sarkic Cult. This will save you a lot of work and stress.

3) You need to define what the humanoid can do better. Telepathy and mental compulsion are different abilities; if it can read minds that works well with the story. A telepathic caveman is a great idea, by the way.

4) Other than that, it looks like you are looking more at a Tale than an actual article. If done as an article, including the information about the spy and its resolution needs to be included as a very clinical addendum, with just the facts. So keep that in mind if you end up writing this up.

5) Also, it's "trait".

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: Conehead
item.content:encoded:
1) Keep in mind that you need about two weeks between posts.

2) In terms of what it is and what it can do, this is an interesting idea. However, it doesn't appear to have a reason for being; it just is. This is sort of why you need to look at the hook; it has to have something that draws in the crowd.

There are two options: Either fit it into the ecology of the universe as a whole give it some sort of symbolic purpose. It's can be a carnivore or a hunter of some sort that is looking for something. It doesn't need to be looking for something to eat; it could be looking for sources of magic or the exotic particles it needs to live. They could even be pets of someone that for whatever reason (the master let them go, they died, or they could have been captured) have their freedom.

Conversely, they could serve as a living symbol of something. As they can't be looked at or even see themselves without confusing themselves, something linked to vanity would be natural. It's also incomplete; that people don't like the incomplete or things that are missing something could fit into it as well.

Like I said: It's a great idea. We're just lacking a reason to care about it that is missing.

item.title: "Intro to Thaumaturgy" College Textbook
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Page Layout: An initial standard page going over the published editions of the book, and a log of incomplete and poorly copied extracts of the text without magic supposedly due to low quality. Followed by an up-to-date article documenting a edited copy of the tome, with a log of the different corrections made by a disenfranchised undergraduate of the establishment that require the book. Containment procedures allow for the book to be borrowed by approved request.

Elevator Pitch: A secondhand university thaumaturgy textbook which is defunct and a scam, corrected by a angry ex-student (of the institution using it as required reading) to make it functional.

+ Show whatever
- Hide whatever

Central Narrative: The book is drawn to the foundation's attention when it is incredulously found via web-crawlers on online book. It is quickly scrubbed from the website due to Foundation concerns about secrecy. A team of researchers are tasked with tracking down copies of the book but all that can be found are monochrome, poorly reproduced photocopies which are useless assisting thaumaturgical practices.

They receive a package from a disgruntled student of a only to discover it is a textbook for a specific professor who charges $25,000 USD (or relative small fortune) or "a year's servitude to dark forces" for it. The book is covered in angry notes expressing frustration in the inaccuracies of it such as " What am I supposed to use?? Pig's blood or wolf?" and "There's no godsdamn way that is an acceptable salt circle", as well as several corrections in order to make the rituals and magic work as intended. The Foundation reclassifies the published versions as non-anomalous and classifies the only anomalous version to be the corrected one.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The thaumaturgy methods and descriptions in an academic way and the premise that not even magic prevents you from being screwed over by the educational system.

Additional Notes: Would appreciate idea on how the actual corrected book is anomalous and not just containing data that can be used to create anomalies, and any areas of thaumaturgy on the SCP universe I should try and include in the photocopy example extracts?


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: "Intro to Thaumaturgy" College Textbook

So it looks like this article is heading into the deletion range. I know that can often feel baffling or upsetting for a first time writer (trust me, you get used to it!), so please take this feedback as advice on your next SCP! If feedback seems harsh, it’s only because I hate when authors keep making the same mistakes until they give up on the wiki. Keep trying, you’ll get there!

Here are a few pitfalls you fell into:

SCP’s are written in clinical, precise language. This piece reads like prose, when a SCP should read like a formal scientific document. I strongly recommend reading the Clinical Tone Guide. Here are a few examples.

“a small table all the way in the back of the chamber”

“All the way in the back” is a very casual way of describing something. “Small” is imprecise.

“Whatever the wearer believes becomes real, and that's anything. Even accidentally.”

Sentence fragments used for emphasis can work in traditional prose, but are out of place in formal scientific writing.

“SCP-5129 seems to be rather “squared”, as if it was what could only be described as “8-bit”.”

“Seems to be” isn’t a great way to describe a SCP. The fictional reader isn’t interested in what it seems to be, they want to know what it is and what it looks like. If there’s a difference between what it is and what it looks like, that should be clear. Using “rather” is imprecise as well.

Beyond the writing style, the content of the SCP has some more fundamental issues. For one, your containment procedures are pretty overblown. From what I can tell, the glasses are only dangerous if somebody touches them. That makes them about as dangerous as a sample of smallpox or a piece of uranium, which is to say, Safe. Euclid is for objects that are unpredictable and need active containment, whereas this thing is fine as long as you don’t poke it. Lock it in a very secure box and don’t let anybody touch it. If you want to be extremely careful, maybe embed it in a block of plastic first. Bam, done.

There’s no narrative arc or story to this piece. Another commenter addressed this above, but basically, you’ve given us this interesting object that can cause all sorts of mayhem and a few lines of mystery about where it came from, but you haven’t gone anywhere with either premise. It’s all setup, with no conclusion.

Mystery and ambiguity is good, but it should be the sort of thing that leaves the reader asking questions once the story is complete. This piece asks the reader to construct a story purely in their head, but is too vague and open-ended to give us the momentum to get there. The payoff to a story can be a sense of horror or mystery, but it still has to be a payoff.

Hope at least some of this helps. I look forward to reading your next article! The wiki has a pretty high attrition rate, so don’t be too discouraged if it takes a while to get one to stick.


Forum category: Per Page Discussions / Per page discussions
Forum thread: SCP-5129

It looks like you're trying to set up a mystery in your central narrative (how did this man get all these quarters?) but the answer to the mystery isn't particularly interesting (an anomaly that makes quarters out of nothing).

Compare your mystery to something like SCP-5005 (spoilers ahead BTW). One of the mysteries 5005 sets up is "where did this giant magic lamp come from?" and the answer is "it's the lure of a massive anglerfish". Once you know the answer, the complete situation "this town exists in a sea of nothingness because of the light of a giant dead anglerfish's lure" is a lot more interesting than "this guy has a lot of quarters because he has an SCP that makes quarters".

The simplest solution would be changing your anomaly so that there's some deeper implication to making all those quarters. Say, for example, that the anomaly is a machine that grinds cute baby animals into a pulp and then turns them into quarters. Now, your complete situation isn't just "this guy has a lot of quarters because he has an SCP that makes quarters"— it's "this guy has a lot of quarters because he was willing to grind up tons of cute baby animals for money."

item.title: Re: SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Holy cow, I think that was really well done. I'd say try and avoid using the phrase "in which" so much. For example, "SCP-XXXX can sense any biological presence from each direction possible, in which it will enter its predator sequence." I feel as if the usage of the phrase "in which" is your informal crutch. In my opinion, a better phrasing might be "SCP-XXXX can sense any biological presence from any possible direction. When a biological presence is sensed, SCP-XXXX enters a predatory sequence."

I feel like scientists with the Foundation will avoid contextual phrasing like "in which" in order to be as clear as possible. Also, when there are two possible subjects in a sentence the scientist at the Foundation would most likely refer to the SCP directly rather than assume the context makes that obvious. Hence, why I suggested "When it senses a biological presence is sensed, SCP-XXXX enters a predatory sequence." This is a Foundation that deals with thousands of anomalies many of which cause anamolous behavior in the victims themselves, so while it may seem redundant it's important to be as specific as possible.

That would be my main tip, for tightening this up, don't rely on contextual language. Be as thorough and specific as you can. Other than that I personally think you have a great start here and I'm really impressed you slapped that together so quick.

Oh almost forgot, you may want to shorten the sentence that talks about reproduction and use more periods instead of commas. And also, explain why in the containment protocols the Foundation is burning the SCP. Are they attempting to destroy it. Are they overbearing it? Is there an ideal mass for containment they are trying to achieve?

These are just some notes. Keep up the good work, and don't forget to check the guide on how to get more reviewers!

item.title: A Photo Book of Murderers
item.content:encoded:
Idea Post:

Seeking Greenlights: Primarily Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror a lot, Drama/Emotional a good deal, History a little.

Page Layout (Optional): Basic special containment procedures and description followed by how it was obtained, then testing logs, and finally incident reports (maybe).

Elevator Pitch: Photobook slash journal used by a former researcher working at an asylum (the early ’50s to ’70s) studying primarily murderous and violent patients. People who place a photo in the book begin to have their memories and their personalities overwritten with psychotic patients.

Central Narrative: I want to highlight the malpractices and the sickening practices of asylums that studied the brains of ‘psychotic’ individuals. Reports of weird experiments have always been rumored and very few reports survive from these places because some of these acts were perpetrated by leading scientists who used this research to better our understanding of psychology. There are even reports of human sacrifices and brutal use of pagan rituals and some real dark sh. Whether or not these are real stories says what if they were really basically.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What is unique in my opinion are the stories the imprinted patients can tell to people, the horrors they experienced, and how it happened.

Additional Notes: I know there are no factual claims to the horrors of such asylums in real life but I just want to tell the story, please don’t come to tell me why it isn't factual. It's SCP it ain’t meant to be factual it's meant to be fun!

item.title: A House Dividing - idea I'd love critiques/greenlights for
item.content:encoded:
An SCP I've been working on casually, I'd love to get critiques on the idea or if it seems solid

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): SCP research article with addendums about the experiments conducted.

Elevator Pitch: An old, abandoned house in New Hampshire with a room upstairs. If you're in the room and can't reach the door it will snap shut and anyone inside disappears. At the exact same moment, four exact copies of that person or those people, linked through physical experience, are generated in four random places on the planet, with one of them in mortal peril and the rest left to experience the death as an introduction to their new, linked experience.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: the house generates people who share physical experiences, and immediately causes one of them to be placed into a situation where they will die. Some of the experiments done on the room after it's discovery had mixed results, however research would have been paused after a character that I think would be useful for other things would be the sole survivor, the three other copies dying within days of their creation. Outside of the death at the beginning, which shocks many who experience it, the three share physical experiences and can communicate in limited fashion with each other. The Foundation experiments with the SCP, first confirming it's safety as well as confirming the sanity and normality of the copies before making a small team of operators, three copies of the same agent, using the SCP after it's experimentation shows it's safe status. That status is revoked when the second person sent through, a higher level operator specializing in Keter Class wet work, becomes the 'sole survivor.' Rather than experiencing a coming together of support and love of his other copies after grieving together, creating a unit far more capable than most, the Sole Survivor experiences their death three times and has a mental breakdown, joining the Chaos.

I have more details/ideas written out as a draft of sorts if you want a link.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: a house in the middle of nowhere that creates linked copies of people random places around the planet and connects their physical experiences.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: It just doesn't feel, "SCP" enough.
item.content:encoded:
Oh No! When editing I took out the lines where I explained what I meant by "encourages you to act on your intrusive thoughts!" So, intrusive thoughts are thoughts that you have impulsively. More often than not these thoughts are violent. People who have been affected by this "magic earworm" have committed acts from strange but harmless behavior all the way up to homicide and self-mutilation. This was actually inspired by something that happened to me the other day. I was cooking and chopping onions and I was singing a song in my head, when an intrusive thought popped up and said "chop your finger off." I started singing "chop your finger off" to the tune of the song that was stuck in my head. I feel so dumb for leaving out the explanation. I was erasing fluff lines to stay under the word count but I must have erased the wrong ones.

Also, I'm glad you asked about if it can appear randomly. Yes it absolutely can. That is how the phenomenon starts in Patient 0, seemingly at random. The Foundation has contained at least a dozen outbreaks in the past, all in different areas around the world. Usually, these outbreaks are 5-10 years apart from each other and leads credence to the "phenomenon theory." However, the past three outbreaks have all been within the past three years. The staff that believes in the "entity theory "believes the entity is going through a sort of molting period, they believe that this entity feeds on sanity and is about to evolve. So it requires more sustenance and is moving at a much faster rate. In the original findings, people who had the "Jukebug" could not transmit it through recordings, and it was safe to record any singing the afflicted did. However within the past three years, the "Jukebug" phenomenon or entity has evolved to be able to spread through audio and visual recording, so the Foundation has revoked clearance for recording.

I know it seems like a lot I left out in the pitch, however I wanted the basics explained first, which I apparently failed to do. Thank you for your input and for taking the time to read this.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: Conehead
item.content:encoded:
This is one of those bizarre ideas I believe definitely belongs on this site at some point. I love the creativity and thought that you put into this. I know this is just an idea critique forum, but if you're seeking green light, my suggestion to you would be to work on your clinical tone and your grammar. For example, "Weirdly enough, it has no body parts except for limbs and the torso, and head. The bottom of its feet where you would usually find paws, is just more fur." This could be written in a way that makes it stronger, "The entity posses all four limbs, but lacks extremities such as paws. Instead the legs end in stubs, balanced on balled up, matted fur. The entity also lacks any visible orifices, or genitalia. This implies the anomaly lacks any digestive track or endocrine system typical of a domesticated canine."

Because the idea is so bizarre and frankly a little funny/cute, I think the best way to get this SCP ready for green light is to rework your idea presentation. Show us you can make this idea draft work in that clinical tone as best as possible to amplify the strengths of your idea.

I truly hope to be scrolling through the articles and stumble across this one day. Thank you for sharing!

item.title: Re: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5127 (Also known as The Cannibal) will eat anything within sight. However, it is worried to eat things around other humans. It appears to be a tall white figure with a very skinny stomach. It’s face features eye sockets that are completely black and a large mouth with shark-like teeth. When it is around humans (as previously mentioned) it gets worried and it’s eye sockets begin to look angry. It gets rid of humans by breathing out air that causes them to open the door and attempt to let the scp free. The human who breathed in the air then kills them self (see incident 5127-A). The creature can eat a full metal door within 15 seconds. As such, we have made a door made out of diamond. The creature eats the diamond door within a 15 day period. The door must be replaced within 10 days as it is then possible for the creature to escape. The creature seems to like wood. As such, we give it 500 planks of wood a day. A human who attempts to harm the creature is eaten by it.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Well, to start I really like the name, Arkansas Creek Walker. I think that's really unique and totally sounds like a cryptid people would believe in, in the Arkansas region. I personally would be fascinated to read more about this. That being said- I think this is really similar to SCP-906, right on down to the tenacity of chasing prey. I think what would make your SCP stand out from 906 would be if the swarm had one single, sentient consciousness.

The difference between a hive mind and single, sentient consciousness would be something like the following:

Hive mind: "Look out, it's a swarm of bugs shaped like a man."
Single mind: " Look out, it's a man, made out of bugs."

However, once you move into the single-mind side of things you start to risk X-Man syndrome. So keep an eye out for that.
As for what should be the cause of this, I grew up in Alaska. In my native culture we had this legend of 3 brothers who were kidnapped by a cannibal giant in the woods. The first two brothers were eaten but the third brother killed the giant and burned his body. The ashes flew into the sky and became the mosquitos. Maybe, that's something you could work with.

Anyhow, I really do like this idea and I'm very interested to see where you take it!

item.title: SCP - The Infinite Quarter
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-#### “The Infinite Quarter” is a 2019 San Antonio Mission Texas Quarter with the head side scratched out with a unknown instrument. The quarter seems like an average coin but when left unobserved the coin will start to rapidly multiply until observed or all open space is occupied. All other instances of the scp do not share the same anomalous duplication ability as the main coin and will only share the ability of ceasing duplication when the coins are observed though if one were to observe a duplicated instance of the coin and not the original coin it will not stop the original from duplicating.

Central Narrative: The coin would of first been discovered when foundation agents caught wind of a man who seemed to of out of the blue came into a fortune oddly enough in quarters. Upon investigating and obvious administration of amnestic, they discovered a shoe box completely full of quarters. It wasn’t until the agent investigating the box looked away and then back to discover that the box had begun to overflow with quarters before stopping. After finding the anomalous coin they brought it to the foundation and contain it in a specially made plastic case big enough to fit a single quarter.

** Hook/Attention-Grabber:** All duplicated instances of the coin will be in perfect condition and not sharing any of the scratch marks on the head side of the coin like the original does. I had also thought to make it so that the actual original coin is always the easiest to spot as to make it more easier to be observed to warrant its duplication stopping when viewed.

** Additional notes:** possible idea is the scp foundation will sometimes use this scp for possible funding for resources and the like.
